newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs get on with Germans but not Gypsies - poll.
newsitem.headline: Czechs get on with Germans but not Gypsies - poll.

text.p: Czechs have few problems in dealings with Germans, even though Prague and Bonn have spent two years negotiating a declaration aimed at resolving mistrust dating from World War Two, an opinion poll showed on Wednesday.
But the poll, conducted by the state-funded IVVM agency, showed more than two thirds of respondents described their relationships with gypsies as bad.

In the poll, conducted in the first week of November, 74 percent said their relations with the citizens of neighbouring Germany were either good or neutral, while just 19 percent described them as bad.

On Tuesday a draft was leaked of the declaration, in which Bonn expresses regret for the Nazi occupation and Prague reciprocates over injustice committed to innocent people during the post-war expulsion of around 2.5 million ethnic Germans.
The declaration is expected to be initialled on December 20 and signed in Prague in late January by Chancellor Helmut Kohl and his Czech counterpart Vaclav Klaus.
But feelings were different towards the Czech Republic's gypsy minority which complains of widespread racism and which has suffered vitriolic attacks in parliament by far-right politicians.
Just under 70 percent of respondents said their personal relations with gypsies were bad, while 20 percent were neutral and a mere five percent said they were good.

The Czech Republic's 250,000 gypsies are its largest ethnic minority. They have been persecuted for hundreds of years and are still banned from many bars, restaurants and public swimming pools. An estimated 70 percent are unemployed.
Citizens of the former Soviet Union, the Balkans and Vietnamese all had disapproval ratings above 40 percent while just five percent said they had bad relations with Jews.
The most positive evaluations went to citizens of former federation partner Slovakia and neighbouring Poland.
The poll was conducted among 1,001 people between November 1 and November 6.
